thread:
Tara: heads up — noticed a bunch of small, high-cost GPU bursts last night that got attributed to 'platform-infra' by the cost-tagging heuristic. Budget alerts blew up for infra owners. :grimacing:

billing-bot: ALERT: untagged GPU spend spike detected. total_spike=1.2k region=us-west1 window=00:47

Ben: Ugh. Do you have sample resource IDs or a query? Could be playground notebooks or a stray job pool.

Tara: here's the query I used (rough):
```
SELECT resource_id, label_owner, created_at, sum(hours * gpu_count) as gpu_hours
FROM usage_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '8 hours' AND region='us-west1'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY gpu_hours desc
LIMIT 20;
```
I can paste a couple resource_ids: rsc-pt-82, rsc-play-443, rsc-notebook-19. They all have label_owner=null and name strings like "notebook-tara-exp" or "experiment-zz-1".

Zane: That matches a failure mode we've seen — the heuristic tries label_owner -> project_key -> name token parsing. For very short lived bursts (<15m) it falls back to the pool default (platform-infra). Our fallback window is currently 2h, so ephemeral notebook allocations are mis-routed.

Marta: Wait so if a notebook spins up for 10m and runs a heavy job, we lose the owner tag and it goes to infra? Can't have infra shouldering dev experiment costs. 

Ben: Quick idea — reduce fallback window and add a name regex that captures common notebook prefixes. Also add a top-n name token classifier that prefers last committer. But we need to check false positives.

Tara: agreed. Also confounding factor: autoscaler-created preemptible pools with no labels get their own pool name which our parser ignores. We should map known autoscaler pools to owning teams.

Zane: I pulled the heuristic code. Relevant snippet: 
```
# pseudo
owner = labels.get('owner') or labels.get('project') or infer_from_name(name)
if not owner and now - created_at < INTERVAL_2H:
    owner = pool_default
```
We should change INTERVAL_2H -> INTERVAL_10M and add a simple regex list: `notebook|playground|experiment|devlab` to bias toward the invoking user when available.

Marta: What's the risk? Could a noisy script fake a notebook name to steal charge?

Zane: small. We'll tolerate some noise for better attribution. We can flag changes for 7 days and run a sampling comparison.

Ben: Operational plan: 1) create a feature flagged PR to  reduce fallback window and add regex; 2) run dry-run attribution on last 30 days and produce a diff report; 3) decide retro allocations for amounts misattributed > $200.

Tara: I'll own the retro allocation review with finance if you push the diff report to /shared/finance/tmp. Also please surface a list of top 10 resource_ids that flip owner after the heuristic change.

Zane: Will draft PR today, add unit tests, and run the sampling job. Estimated time: 3-4 hours for PR + 2h for sampling job.

billing-bot: NOTE: created ticket FIN-3126 for retro allocation workflow. Reference: #1799123456

Marta: For transparency can we add a Grafana panel showing 'heuristic confidence' per resource? Even a simple boolean for owner_inferred vs explicit_label.

Ben: yes, add a boolean tag to ingestion stream `owner_inferred=true|false`. We'll ingest to billing-events and wire to Grafana.

Tara: thanks all. Please @me when PR is up. Also small ask: can we emit an alert when a single resource > $250 in <1h with owner_inferred=true so finance can triage sooner?

Zane: good call. I'll add that to the sampling job output and to the alert rules.

Ben: I'll review PR once it's up. 

Tara: leaving this here — we're hitting infra owners' budgets nightly, so sooner the better. :pray:

Marta: noted. Follow-up: schedule 30m to review diff and decide retro at 10am PST tomorrow?

Tara: works for me.

billing-bot: REMINDER: FIN-3126 assigned to Tara, due_date=2026-03-25

Zane: PR link: (draft) github.com/redwood/repo/compare/heuristic-owner-short-window — ping when CI passes.

Tara: will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
